# kala_cases (Data Source)

Lists cases in Kala.

Kala names this entity three ways -- "project" on webapiv2, "job" in internal endpoint names, "case" in responses. This provider says **case** throughout.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# `active` selects a SET rather than narrowing one. Kala's archived and
# non-archived cases are DISJOINT, and no single call returns both, so reading
# everything takes two blocks.

data "kala_cases" "active" {
  # active = true   # the default
}

data "kala_cases" "archived" {
  active = false
}

output "all_cases" {
  value = concat(data.kala_cases.active.cases, data.kala_cases.archived.cases)
}

# Filter by customer company. Applied client-side over the case list, which
# carries the company as text but no customer id — so this is string matching,
# not a join. Pair it with kala_customer when you need the id.
data "kala_cases" "for_customer" {
  customer_company = "Bag End Ltd"
}

# An explicit empty string selects cases with no customer, such as internal
# projects. Leaving it unset applies no filter at all.
data "kala_cases" "internal_projects" {
  customer_company = ""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Which set of cases to return. Defaults to `true`.

**These are disjoint sets, not a narrowing filter.** `true` returns only non-archived cases; `false` returns only archived ones. Kala offers **no single call that returns both**, so retrieving every case requires two `kala_cases` blocks, one per value.
- `customer_company` (String) Return only cases whose customer company matches exactly, ignoring case.

**Applied client-side.** The case list carries the customer's company as text but no customer id, so this is string matching rather than a join: it will not follow a renamed company, and two customers sharing a company name are indistinguishable here. Use `kala_customer` when you need the id.

Deliberately not pushed into `search`, which is a broad text match over case names as well as customer fields, so narrowing with it could drop cases that genuinely match.

Set to `""` to select cases with **no** customer, such as internal projects. Leaving it unset applies no filter.
- `include_contact_details` (Boolean) Expose the customer email and phone denormalised onto each case. Off by default; this is personal data and everything here is written to state.
- `page_size` (Number) Records fetched per request while paginating.
- `search` (String) Free-text filter applied upstream. Matches case names and customer fields.

### Read-Only

- `cases` (Attributes List) The cases returned. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cases))
- `complete` (Boolean) Whether the read covered every case in the requested set. **False means this list is a subset.**
- `total` (Number) How many cases the requested set holds, as reported upstream.

<a id="nestedatt--cases"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cases`

Read-Only:

- `address` (String) Site address.
- `archived` (Boolean) Whether this case is archived. Derived from which set was requested, not from a response field: the list endpoint's own `isFinished` tracks archived-ness rather than completion and disagrees with the detail endpoint.
- `customer_company` (String) Customer company name.
- `customer_email` (String) Customer email address. **Null unless `include_contact_details` is set** -- contact data is personal data and everything exposed here is written to Terraform state.
- `customer_name` (String) Customer contact name, denormalised onto the case.
- `customer_phone` (String) Customer phone number. **Null unless `include_contact_details` is set** -- contact data is personal data and everything exposed here is written to Terraform state.
- `economy_case_number` (String) The e-conomic case number. In practice this **mirrors `number`**, including on Kala-native internal projects that have no e-conomic counterpart.
- `favorite` (Boolean) Whether the case is flagged as a favourite.
- `id` (Number) Kala's internal case id. This is the value tasks reference via `case_id`.
- `internal_project` (Boolean) Whether this is an internal project rather than customer work. Internal projects have no customer.
- `name` (String) Case name.
- `number` (String) The case number, e.g. `KA-1`. This is how a case is addressed, and it is a **string** -- distinct from the integer `id`.
- `restricted` (Boolean) Whether access to the case is restricted.
- `sub_text` (String) Secondary descriptive line.
- `zip` (String) Postal code.
